newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 11.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Although the prepared package of measures to support the Czech economy was not supposed to contain an import surcharge, negotiations within the government continue. Most of the coalition is against it, but an import surcharge still carries significant political support.

- The proposal for an agreement, which should have meant the end of the battle between the Health Ministry and large drug distributors (AVEL), did not please the distributors. AVEL said the ministry is requesting that distributors provide hospitals with drugs even when they do not receive payment.

- Government no-interest loans of 200,000 crowns for organising new housing will begin in the middle of this year, when the cabinet-approved programme for deregulating rents and energy prices goes into effect.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Czech National Bank will decrease minimum reserves requirements, which commercial banks must keep in the central bank, to 9.5 percent from 11.5, effective May 8.

- Shareholders of Chemapol Group approved the cancellation of employee shares in its meeting yesterday. Every employee share at a nominal value of 2,000 crowns each will be replaced by two basic shares with a nominal value of 1,000 crowns each.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Vladimir Rulovcak, deputy Finance Minister, resigned from his position yesterday of his own accord. He was led to this decision by a wave of strong criticism in connection to the case of C S Fond.
- Teachers dissatisfied with their wages will hold a demonstration on Saturday on Old Town Square in Prague. About 10,000 teachers from all regions of the country are expected to participate.
- Eurotel increased its revenue by about 50 percent last year to 4.64 billion crowns compared to 2.98 billion in 1995. Its net profits dropped to 435 million crowns compared to 566 million in 1995.
- Plzensky Prazdroj sold 910,000 hectolitres of beer during the first quarter of this year, a year-on-year, increase of 22.3 percent.

PRAVO - Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar added another condition to his request for an apology from President Vaclav Havel for remarks made about Meciar in an interview. Meciar announced that he will only meet with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus after the Czech Republic returns 10 tonnes of gold to Slovakia.
- The holding company Interkontakt Group, the leading retail group in the country, is planning its debut on the capital market this year, according to a spokesperson for the group, Vlasta Krejcova.

- The forced administrator of Agrobanka, Jiri Klumpar, offered the union of minority shareholders on Thursday an end to forced administration if the shareholders are willing to issue new shares for the bank worth 6.5 billion crowns.
